Full summary: Stage 2 (D2): persisted blackboard lifecycle — status resolved with audit fields in both backends, twining_resolve tool, twining_record resolves[], union resolution predicate, dismiss tombstones with reason
Decisions: Chose to register twining_resolve on the DEFAULT surface rather than mirroring its sibling twining_dismiss's full-surface gating — the field defect was precisely that the everyday surface offered no exit from the open lane, and resolve is constructive (preserves the record) while dismiss is destructive; this deviates from the plan's mirror-sibling assumption deliberately; Chose to keep lifecycle status inside the entry JSON blob over adding a sqlite status column — no SQLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump, no downgrade hazard, and the open lane is already computed in JS over full entries; Chose first-resolve-wins idempotency for re-resolves — the audit stamp records the actual resolution event; overwriting it on repeat calls would falsify history; Chose to implement dismissal tombstones in the tool handler appending to the archive jsonl rather than a soft-delete status — zero read-path changes, the archiver's internal dismiss stays tombstone-free, and the compactor's exact-signature matching preserves tombstone lines
Findings: Explicitly resolved needs/warnings now DRAIN via the archiver — the #40 exemption no longer shields them once resolved; intended behavior change, must be called out in CHANGELOG and field memo; twining_record with resolves[] both back-references (old predicate) and explicitly resolves (new predicate) — double coverage so pre-2.7 consumers of relates_to still agree
